findings.message: Withdrawal assumes that any record missing from the push was deleted from the repo. The server accepts `withdrawMissing: true` with `records: []`. The CI script then sends one empty batch: `Math.max(records.length, 1)` makes one batch, and `withdrawMissing` is true because `batches.length === 1`. The reader returns [] when `.specclaw/changes` doesn't exist (`folders()` → `existsSync ? … : []`), so 'could not read any changes' looks the same as 'every change was deleted'. Fix: the server should refuse `withdrawMissing` when `records` is empty, and ideally when the push would withdraw most of the project's live specclaw proposals. `specclaw-sync-ci.mjs` should stop with an error, not push, when the main read returns no records.
findings.scenario: A merge to main moves `.specclaw/changes` (or the job runs from the wrong root). The workflow fires on the `.specclaw/**` path, `payload()` returns 0 records, and the CI posts `{records: [], withdrawMissing: true}`. Every main-synced proposal that isn't Released gets `meta.withdrawn = true`, and the job goes green with 'N withdrawn'.

findings.message: This diff adds a second withdrawal rule, `withdrawable`, and it disagrees with the self-sync's rule in `sync/import.ts:82-90`. The self-sync still withdraws any leftover row: it doesn't check for Released, whether the default branch last synced the row, or whether the commit is newer. `refOf` is also copied between `push.ts:71` and `import.ts:32`. The README presents the self-sync as the same sync for a self-hosted amax ('skips duplicate numbers the same way'). Fix: move the withdrawal predicate and `refOf` into one shared function and use it on both paths.
findings.scenario: CON-076 was created by a push from `specclaw/076-late-fees`, so `meta.source = specclaw/076-late-fees@…`, and its folder isn't on main yet. A `sync_specclaw` push from main with `withdrawMissing` leaves it alone. The 039 self-sync of the same main tree withdraws it. The self-sync also withdraws a Released proposal whose folder was removed, which the push refuses to do.

findings.message: The change-number check is a later step in the `review-gate` job. When `check-review-gate.mjs` fails, this step is skipped, so the PR never learns about a reused number until the gate passes. Run it as its own job, or add `if: always()`, so its result is reported independently.
findings.scenario: A fork PR with no finished review loop that also adds `088-agent-draft`: CI reports only the review-gate failure. The number clash shows up only after the review is done.

findings.message: The skip line is built only from the dirs in the current batch. When CI or the plugin splits records at 200 and two folders sharing a number land on either side of the split, each batch skips its own folder on the client's `duplicate` flag but names only that one folder: 'two changes numbered 200: 200-a'. That contradicts the message's own claim of two changes. Put the other dir in the record (e.g. `duplicateOf`), or keep a number's records in the same batch when batching.
findings.scenario: 201 changes where 200-a and 200-b are records 200 and 201. Batch 1 warns 'two changes numbered 200: 200-a', and batch 2 warns '…: 200-b'.

findings.message: The mock says that without its secrets 'The job ends neutral, never green-skipped'. `run()` returns 0 in that case, so the job is green with a notice, which is what the README and the test expect. Fix the mock text to match.
findings.scenario: No secrets set → `run()` returns 0 → the Actions job shows green, not neutral.

findings.message: Refused and Needs you both use `chip warn`, so the two can't be told apart by colour. The mock uses `chip bad` for Refused. Push rows written before 0020 default `needs_review` to false, so an old push that skipped a held or unreadable record now shows as 'Applied'.
findings.scenario: A refused push and a push that hit a duplicate number show the same yellow chip on the Repo sync card.

findings.message: A duplicate pair that is already on main sets `needsReview` on every push. The CI pushes after every merge, so AMX (with its 062, 074 and 075 pairs) gets a new 'Needs you' row on the Repo sync card for each merge until someone renumbers them, and those rows bury the pushes that do need a person. Consider flagging a known pair only when it first appears, or only when the push is listed for another reason.
findings.scenario: Ten merges to amax's main in a day → ten 'Needs you' rows, each listing the same three duplicate numbers.

findings.message: The check groups by number over `headDirs` only. A folder that is on the base tip but not on the PR branch (main moved on after the PR branched) is never compared. The check then passes a PR that reuses the number, and the merge creates a duplicate. Fix: compare each added folder against the union of base and head folders, e.g. `byNumber([...new Set([...baseDirs, ...headDirs])])`.
findings.scenario: After the PR branched, main gains 090-audit-filters. The PR adds 090-invoice-export and isn't rebased. base = [...,'090-audit-filters'], head = [...,'090-invoice-export'] → head has one folder for 090 → failures = [] → the merge leaves two 090 folders, and every later sync skips FLT-090.

findings.message: A sync that didn't run reports as a passing job. With no secrets, or only some of them, `run` returns 0, so the job is green. The mock says this case 'ends neutral, never green-skipped', and the code contradicts it. A partial configuration (e.g. AMAX_URL set but the key missing or expired) is also treated as 'not set up' instead of failing (B6). Fix: exit 0 with the notice only when none of the three secrets is set. When some are set and others aren't, exit non-zero. Then align the mock and READMEs with whatever the job actually does.
findings.scenario: An admin rotates the credential and deletes AMAX_SYNC_API_KEY, leaving AMAX_URL and AMAX_SYNC_ACT_FOR → every merge to main shows a green 'specclaw sync' job, and the board silently stops updating.

findings.message: Duplicate detection depends on the client sending both folders. A plugin installed before 089 still merges records by number, so it sends one record per shared number. `duplicateNumbers` then sees one dir and no flag, syncs that folder over the 'frozen' key, and breaks AC-9's 'leaves that key's proposal untouched'. Consider refusing pushes whose records lack the `duplicate` field (an old reader), or recording the reader version.
findings.scenario: A developer on an old plugin runs /amax:sync-specclaw on main, which has 074-a and 074-b → one record 074 (whichever the old reader kept) is applied → FLT-074's title and phase flip to that folder's state.
